{{c|''He continueth his talke to the Pharisees; shewing that they and al other that wil not enter in by him, are wolues: and that they which heare them, are not the true sheepe. 11 But that him self is the good Pastor, and therfore to saue the sheepe from these wolues, he wil yeld his life, which otherwise no might of theirs could take from him: foretelling also his Resurrection, and vocation of the Gentils. 22 Againe an other time, he telleth these Iewes openly, that they are not of his sheepe, and that no might of theirs shal take from him his true sheepe, because he is God, euen as his Father is God. 31 Which by his miracles and by Scripture he sheweth to be no blasphemie: and they in vaine seeking to stone and to apprehend him, 40 he goeth out to the place where Iohn Baptist had giuen open witnes of him.''}} {{dropinitial|A|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial A, two satyrs.png|imgsize=185px|fl={{verse|chapter=10|verse=1}}}}MEN, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō Tuesday in whitson weeke.}}amen I say to you, he that entreth not by the doore into the folde of the sheepe, but {{sup|‖}} climeth vp an other vvay: he is {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ The theefe, is the Heretike specially, & any other that vnlawfully breake in vpon the sheepe to kil & destroy them by false doctrine and otherwise.}}∷ a theefe and a robber. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=2}}† But he that entreth by the doore, is the Pastor of the sheepe. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=3}}† To this man the porter openeth: & the sheepe heare his voice: and he calleth his ovvne sheepe by name, and leadeth them forth. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=4}}† And vvhen he hath let forth his ovvne sheepe, he {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ That is the fashion of Iewrie & other countries, signifying that the shepheard or Pastor must teach the sheepe, and not they him.}}∷ goeth before them: and the sheepe folovv him, because they knovv his voice. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=5}}† But a stranger they folovv not, but flee from him: because they knovv not the voice of strangers. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=6}}† This prouerbe {{sc|Iesvs}} said to them. But they knevv not vvhat he spake to them.

{{verse|chapter=10|verse=7}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore said to them againe, Amen, amen I say to you, that I am the doore of the sheepe. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=8}}† And hovv many soeuer haue come, are theeues and robbers: but the sheepe heard them not. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=9}}† I am the doore. By me if any enter, he shal be saued: and he shal goe in and shal goe out, and shal finde pastures. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=10}}† The theefe commeth not but to steale and kil and destroy. I came that they may haue life, and may haue more aboundantly.⊣ {{verse|chapter=10|verse=11}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō the 2 Sunday after Easter, and for S. Thomas of Canterburie, ''Decemb. 29.''}}I am the {{sup|‖}} good Pastor. The good Pastor giueth his life for his sheepe. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=12}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Esa. 40, 11. Ezec. 34, 23.''}}* But the hireling and he that is not the Pastor, vvhose ovvne the sheepe are not, seeth the vvoulfe comming, and leaueth the sheepe, and fleeth: and the vvoulfe raueneth, and disperseth the sheepe. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=13}}† And the hireling {{sup|‖}} fleeth because he is a hireling: and he hath no care of the sheepe. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=14}}† I am the good Pastor: and I knovv mine, and mine knovv me. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=15}}† As the Father knovveth me, and I knovv the Father: and {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Christes death was so necessarie for the flocke, that when he might haue escaped, he voluntarily offered him self to death for his flocke.}}∷ I yeld my life for my sheepe. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=16}}† And c other sheepe I haue that are not of this folde: them also I must bring, and they shal heare my voice, and there shal be made {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Ezec. 37, 24.''}}* one folde and one Pastor.⊣ {{verse|chapter=10|verse=17}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ He meaneth the Church of the Gentils.}}∷ Therfore the Father loueth me: because I yeld my life, that I may take it againe. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=18}}† No man taketh it avvay from me: but {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Esa. 53, 7.''}}* I yeld it of my self. and I haue povver to yeld it: and I haue povver to take it againe. This commaundement I receiued of my father.

{{verse|chapter=10|verse=19}}† A dissension rose againe among the Ievves for these vvordes. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=20}}† And many of them said, He hath a deuil and is mad: vvhy heare you him? {{verse|chapter=10|verse=21}}† Others said, These are not the vvordes of one that hath a deuil. can a deuil open the eies<noinclude>{{rh|||of}}</noinclude>
